messages:
From: Susan Jenkins <susan.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com, security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request to execute DPA + breach notification windows

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal and security from our side are ready to move forward but want to confirm a couple of items before we sign the DPA:

1) Breach notice timing: our security team asks for "initial customer notice" within 24 hours of customer-impacting data exposure and a full forensic report within 30 days.
2) Subprocessor visibility: we need a 30-day advance notice of any new subprocessors and the ability to review for high-risk subprocessors.
3) Cross-border transfers: confirmation you can rely on SCCs and our preference is a clause referencing documented transfer mechanisms.

I've attached our latest redlines (see Acme_DPA_redlines_v3.docx). Can Redwood accept these or propose counter language?

We'd prefer DocuSign to keep execution clean — can you route to your legal for one-signature execution and loop in procurement for countersign?

Susan Jenkins
Director, Legal Operations
Acme Analytics

Attachments: Acme_DPA_redlines_v3.docx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Susan Jenkins <susan.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request to execute DPA + breach notification windows

Thanks Susan — appreciate the clarity and the redlines. High level response below and then internal notes.

- DocuSign: yes, we can execute via DocuSign. I'll initiate the envelope once we agree language.
- Breach notification: redlines requesting "initial customer notice within 24 hours" is workable for confirmed customer-impacting incidents, but we need to preserve a short investigatory window for detection and false positives. Proposed compromise we usually offer: initial notice within 48 hours of detection for incidents requiring customer notice; "critical incidents" (confirmed exfiltration of customer data) get a 24-hour initial notice. Full forensic report within 30 days (we can commit to a 30-day preliminary report and a targeted 90-day final if deeper forensics required).
- Subprocessors: we can provide 30-day notice for new subprocessors but cannot offer opt-out (that would break operations). We can include a right to review and request mitigation for high-risk subprocessors with a 30-day cure period.
- Transfers: we rely on SCCs + documented safeguards; if you have specific in-country requirements we can discuss.

I'll loop in Legal to propose explicit redline language. If Acme can accept the 48/24 critical carve, we'll move to DocuSign today and aim to have the envelope out by EOD.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: acknowledged Acme_DPA_redlines_v3.docx

Subject: Fwd: Request to execute DPA + breach notification windows

Laura / Olga / Aditya —

Please see Acme's redlines attached. Key asks: 24-hour initial notice for customer-impacting exposures, 30-day forensic report, 30-day subprocessor notice and opt-out language.

I recommend the following counter redlines (short bullets):
- 48-hour initial notice for incidents requiring customer notice; 24-hour for confirmed critical exfiltration.
- 30-day preliminary forensic report; final report within 90 days as necessary.
- 30-day notice for new subprocessors with right-to-review (no unilateral opt-out); include escalation path to Security for high-risk requests.
- Add a DocuSign go-live clause: envelope to be sent after legal sign-off, procurement will countersign.

Can Legal produce a tracked redline to send back to Acme? We want to avoid back-and-forth on the notice window; if Acme insists on 24h across-the-board we need exec escalation.

On the DocuSign front, I can loop in our vendor contact (Kyle Brooks) to request expedited envelope creation once redlines are accepted.

Thanks —Marcus

From: ACME Legal Team <legal@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Jenkins <susan.jenkins@acme.com>, security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-06-19T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — carve for 24h and subprocessor opt-out

Marcus —

We reviewed your proposed compromise. Acme is firm on the 24-hour initial notice for customer-impacting incidents. Our rationale is regulator-facing: we need to show customers and regulators that notice was made promptly once impact is known.

Regarding subprocessors, the opt-out gives us contractual leverage with our own customers; however, we're open to the right-to-review + mitigation path if Redwood will commit to a security-led escalation and provide a named contact for subprocessor risk reviews.

Proposed ask from Acme: if Redwood cannot accept 24h universally, accept 24h for any incident meeting our "customer-impact" definition in Section A.3 of the attached redlines and provide a 48-hour window only when further internal triage is required (documented with timeline).

We would like to keep execution via DocuSign and have procurement countersign. Please provide a tracked redline by EOD tomorrow so we can review.

—ACME Legal

Attachment: Acme_DPA_redlines_v3.docx

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — internal suggested counter

Marcus / team —

Draft tracked changes prepared. Key language I added (high level):

1) Notification timing (new Section 6.2): "Redwood will provide initial written notice to Customer within forty-eight (48) hours of detection of a security incident that requires Customer notification. For incidents meeting the Customer-Impact criteria set forth in Section A.3 (e.g., confirmed unauthorized access resulting in exfiltration of Customer Data), Redwood will provide initial notice within twenty-four (24) hours of confirmation. Redwood will document any investigatory delay and provide evidence of the steps taken during the investigatory window."

2) Subprocessors: "Redwood will provide Customer with written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to engaging a new Subprocessor. Customer may submit a written objection during such notice period specifying a legitimate, documented security reason. Redwood will engage in good-faith discussions and, if the parties are unable to agree, either party may escalate to senior security leadership for resolution. Customer's ability to terminate for the addition of a Subprocessor is limited to a material-breach termination right within thirty (30) days of execution of the Subprocessor agreement."

3) Attach evidence matrix (evidence_matrix.xlsx) to the DPA as Appendix B for SOC2 artifacts and KMS/HSM detail.

I recommend we send this tracked redline back to Acme with a short cover note and then route to DocuSign. If Acme refuses to accept differential (24/48) language we will need an exec exception to push 24h universal.

—Olga

Attachment: tracked_redline_DPA_vR1.docx, evidence_matrix.xlsx
